'''Robert G. Greenler''' was an American physicist. His research centered on the optical properties of surfaces. Greenler received his B.S. from the [[University of Rochester]] and a Ph.D. from [[Johns Hopkins University]]. He taught [[physics]] at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]] from 1962-1992.<ref name="osa">[http://www.osa.org/history/biographies/robert-g--greenler/ Robert G. Greenler], The Optical Society of America]</ref> He became professor emeritus of the same university after his retirement.

Greenler was president of the [[Optical Society of America]] in 1987.<ref>{{cite news | title = Past Presidents of the Optical Society of America| publisher =Optic Society of America | url =http://www.osa.org/aboutosa/leadership/pastpresidents/default.aspx }}</ref> He was the recipient of the [[Robert A. Millikan award]] in 1988.

He is well known for his popular lectures on physics "[[The Science Bag]]", which he started with colleague [[Glenn Schmieg]] in 1973. "The Science Bag" is a family friendly lecture series on every Friday evening and one Sunday a month at [[UW-Milwaukee]] Physics Building. In its 30-year existence the program attracted a cumulative audience of over 140,000 people.<ref name="osa" />

==Awards==
*University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee Ernest Spaights Plaza Award
*Optical Society of America Esther Hoffman Beller Award.
* [[Esther Hoffman Beller Medal]] 1993
*American Association of Physics Teachers Robert A. Millikan award, 1988
Elected Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science
